transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Stop the machine immediately and unplug it from the wall socket. Do not use the appliance again until a qualified engineer has checked it, as there is an electrical hazard with water on the floor. Once it is safe to do so (switched off and unplugged), you can check if the leak is coming from the detergent drawer at the top or from the bottom front filter area. This will help the engineer identify the cause.
ok I'm panicking a bit, I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now. the fuse box is in the hall and the floor's dry there, should I go and switch it off first?

Yes, please go and switch off the circuit at the fuse box immediately. Do not touch the washing machine or the plug until you have done this. Once the power is isolated and it is safe for you to approach the appliance (dry hands, dry floor), check if water is dripping from the small flap at the bottom left of the machine front (the filter cover). This will help identify where the leak is coming from.
ok going to switch it off at the fuse box now. the water's run back towards the socket and the floor under the plug is wet. what do I do after that?

Once you have switched off the power at the fuse box and it is safe for you to approach (dry hands, dry floor), place some old towels or an empty bucket under the bottom left corner of the machine. Open the small flap at the bottom left (the filter cover), unscrew the filter slowly to let any water drain out into a bucket or onto the towels. Is the water coming from inside the machine via that filter area? This will help identify if it is a blocked filter, a loose hose, or a pump failure.

ok power's off at the fuse box now. the water is mostly at the front under the door, not the bottom left flap. the machine is full of water and too heavy for me to pull out on my own. should I still open the filter?

No, do not open the filter. Because there is an active electrical hazard (water near the plug) and the leak appears to be internal (under the door rather than from a loose filter cap), this needs a qualified engineer to safely disconnect the machine, drain it properly, and diagnose the source of the leak. Please leave the power off at the fuse box and do not attempt to use or move the appliance until an engineer attends.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
